coverage: All 25 PNGs inspected individually with view_image; no mapping, sources, outside-directory files or other reviews opened.
recognition: View 05 tentatively recognized as StarCraft II; views 11 and 18 as Company of Heroes. Views 01 and 08 resemble a tactical planning game without confident exact identification. Recognizable recurring images received the same scores as in the preceding packet.

view-01.png.evidence: Detailed produce stalls, carts, warm light and grounded shadows make a coherent market. Colored planning lines remain distinct, but small people and many icons compete at phone size.

view-02.png.evidence: Fixed objective bars preserve the play area; teal waves and carrier deck fittings establish the scene. Soft aircraft edges, limited shadow depth and stern overlap reduce precision.

view-03.png.evidence: Top objectives and open green terrain keep the aircraft visible. Roof panels and tree shading help, but broad flat grass, weak field differentiation and a hard beach edge remain basic.

view-04.png.evidence: Crisp deck rim and a more elevated island with dark sides give the carrier stronger volume. Restrained sea flecks preserve clarity. The long wake visible in other carrier views is absent, reducing motion and water-contact information; player still merges with stern.

view-05.png.evidence: Hot impact core, sparks and beams form a strong focal event amid detailed ships and alien terrain. Dark clustered units merge and the bright blast hides targets.

view-06.png.evidence: Clear top objectives, isolated sharp carrier, deck fixtures and subdued whitecaps give a readable composition. Simple twin wake and limited ocean variation remain; player silhouette merges with stern.

view-07.png.evidence: Sharp aircraft and deck details stand apart from subdued water highlights. Dense near-identical aircraft and soft particles crowd the player at the stern, obscuring action hierarchy.

view-08.png.evidence: Thick walls, varied floors, furniture, warm/cool light and occlusion clearly articulate rooms. Tiny figures and thin planning lines require concentration at this size.

view-09.png.evidence: Crisp aircraft with offset shadows and an elevated shaded carrier island add height cues. The wake is absent compared with similar views, and stern overlaps plus tiny foam-like puffs still weaken player and motion clarity.

view-10.png.evidence: Tree shadows, shoreline stones, softer sand transition and raised hangar edges make the coast more dimensional. Plane remains legible, though nearby rocks compete slightly; large grass and field areas are still plain.

view-11.png.evidence: Wet reflective roads, rubble, directional smoke, rain and lit projectiles create a convincing storm battlefield. Dark tanks and tiny infantry merge with rich ground textures.

view-12.png.evidence: Runway arrow, panelled roofs and top objective bar provide clear hierarchy. Plane overlaps a hangar, grass is repetitive, and beach lacks surf or depth transition.

view-13.png.evidence: Offset aircraft shadows and dark island sides add volume despite soft rendering. The carrier has no long visible wake and a few pale puffs do little to establish water contact; stern overlap persists.

view-14.png.evidence: Shore rocks, shaded trees, elevated roof sides and faint tracks make the airfield richer. Soft edges and repeated shoreline stones feel formulaic; the plane still overlaps a roof and water contact remains minimal.

view-15.png.evidence: Sharp runway and roof edging, tree shadows, muted ocean flecks and separated objective text create a clean layout. Broad plain lawn and uniform sand edge remain schematic.

view-16.png.evidence: Crisp structures, subtle wave flecks and clean objective placement keep the coastal scene clear. Large grass regions and a hard straight sand strip offer limited environmental depth.

view-17.png.evidence: Offset shadows under aircraft and dark carrier-island sides strengthen height cues. Repeated black aircraft shadows add clutter to an already crowded swarm; soft dot particles lack impact hierarchy and long wake is absent.

view-18.png.evidence: Fog recedes through trees and ruins, with tracks, debris, muzzle flashes and smoke integrated into the landscape. Small camouflaged units remain difficult to distinguish.

view-19.png.evidence: Top objective strips separate text from combat; deck fixtures and teal wave pattern add structure. Soft aircraft and particles overlap the carrier and stern, reducing target readability.

view-20.png.evidence: Open composition, fixed objectives and raised shaded island keep the carrier readable. Soft edges limit precision; missing long wake reduces movement cues and surrounding water remains repetitive.

view-21.png.evidence: Stones, deeper tree shadows and raised hangars give the coastal land more dimensional context. Soft image detail and repeated stones limit material quality; large blank grass remains.

view-22.png.evidence: Sharp roof facets, dark wall sides, tree shadows, shoreline stones, faint tracks and sea flecks enrich the airfield without obscuring layout. Plane still overlaps the central hangar; repeated stones and nearly uniform beach lack natural variation.

view-23.png.evidence: Aircraft shadows and raised island improve height perception, while objective bars remain clean. Dense dark duplicate silhouettes and soft particles amplify central clutter, and the absent wake weakens movement cues.

view-24.png.evidence: Sharp aircraft, deck fixtures and restrained ocean highlights improve finish. Player and planes still overlap the carrier; tiny waves can compete with wings, and wake remains simple.

view-25.png.evidence: Sparse carrier scene, fixed objective bars and dark hull outline are easily parsed. Soft deck geometry, thin material detail and broad empty sea limit richness; wake is basic.

general_findings: Scores preserve prior anchors for visually unchanged scenes; no candidate identity or presumed progression was used.
More pronounced aircraft/tree shadows and raised carrier-island/hangar sides improve depth. Shoreline rocks and faint tracks add useful environmental context.

Visible regressions/tradeoffs: long carrier wakes disappear in views 04,09,13,17,20,23 relative to corresponding wake-bearing scenes. This weakens motion and hull-water interaction even though geometric depth improves.
Offset dark aircraft shadows increase clutter in swarm scenes, particularly 17 and 23; they do not resolve the player silhouette merging with the stern.

Highest priorities remain player separation and clear impact hierarchy. Keep improved volumetric structures and land shadows, restore convincing coherent carrier wake/contact effects, and vary shoreline materials beyond evenly repeated rocks.
The rich reference scenes retain a substantial material/lighting advantage; sparse aviation scenes remain more immediately legible but have limited environmental variety.
